<awtsmoosMeluketTranslation heichel="ikar" alias="meluket_translation_en" seriesId="אדר_meluket" postId="BH_POST_1766518917442_theRebbe_735" batchId="meluket-_D7_90_D7_93_D7_A8_meluket__BH_POST_1766518917442_theRebbe_735__p001">
  <section v="0">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>Introductory heading for the Purim maamar of 5713.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">With the help of Heaven.</t>
    <t s="1">Purim</t>
    <t s="2">(Maamar 2)*</t>
    <t s="3">5713</t>
  </section>
  <section v="1">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>The name "Purim" derives from the "pur" (lot), indicating that the essence of the Purim miracle is the lot itself, not just its outcome.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">"Therefore they called these days Purim, after the name of the pur [lot]."1</t>
    <t s="1">And according to what is known2</t>
    <t s="2">that the name of every thing indicates its essence,</t>
    <t s="3">it is understood</t>
    <t s="4">that the fact that they called these days Purim after the name of the pur is because the main aspect of the festival of Purim is the lot</t>
    <t s="5">(pur means the lot3).</t>
    <t s="6">And it needs to be understood</t>
    <t s="7">(as is pointed out in Torah Or, discourse "Zeh"4),</t>
    <t s="8">for at first glance,</t>
    <t s="9">this was not</t>
    <t s="10">[the main5]</t>
    <t s="11">the miracle.</t>
    <t s="12">And furthermore,</t>
    <t s="13">the lot that Haman cast</t>
    <t s="14">(not only was this not the miracle,</t>
    <t s="15">but on the contrary)</t>
    <t s="16">was part of the decree</t>
    <t s="17">[and in the language of the Megillah6:</t>
    <t s="18">"He cast a pur, that is the lot, to destroy them and annihilate them"],</t>
    <t s="19">and from the fact that these days are called Purim after the name of the pur,</t>
    <t s="20">it implies that this</t>
    <t s="21">(the lot)</t>
    <t s="22">is the main aspect of the Purim miracle,</t>
    <t s="23">to the extent that the miracle is named after this.</t>
    <t s="24">And at first glance, it could be explained according to what is stated in the Gemara7</t>
    <t s="25">that when the lot fell in the month of Adar, [Haman] rejoiced</t>
    <t s="26">(Haman)</t>
    <t s="27">with great joy,</t>
    <t s="28">saying, "A lot has fallen for me in the month in which Moshe died,"</t>
    <t s="29">and he did not know that on the seventh of Adar he died and on the seventh of Adar he was born.</t>
    <t s="30">And based on this, it could be said</t>
    <t s="31">that the reason these days are called after the name of the pur is because the miracle of Purim was that the lot fell in the month of Adar,</t>
    <t s="32">the month in which Moshe, the savior of Israel, was born.</t>
    <t s="33">But this explanation is still difficult,</t>
    <t s="34">because from the fact that the festival is called Purim after the name of the pur,</t>
    <t s="35">it implies</t>
    <t s="36">that the connection of the miracle to the pur is</t>
    <t s="37">(not only to the fact that the lot fell in the month of Adar,</t>
    <t s="38">but also)</t>
    <t s="39">to the matter of the pur itself.</t>
    <t s="40">And on the contrary,</t>
    <t s="41">the main miracle was from the aspect of the pur, which is the lot.</t>
    <t s="42">For a lot is a very lofty matter,</t>
    <t s="43">from which the miracle is drawn.</t>
    <t s="44">And that the lot fell on the month of Adar, in which the savior of Israel was born, is</t>
    <t s="45">(like all the matters that occurred in the Purim miracle,</t>
    <t s="46">which are)</t>
    <t s="47">a result of its main essence,</t>
    <t s="48">Purim after the name of the pur.</t>
  </section>
  <section v="2">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>Purim and Yom Kippur are connected through the concept of the lot, both revealing a level above the name Havayah.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">2)</t>
    <t s="1">And this will be understood based on what is explained in Torah Or8</t>
    <t s="2">that Purim and Yom HaKippurim are related to each other9.</t>
    <t s="3">For the explanation of Yom K.</t>
    <t s="4">Purim is like Purim</t>
    <t s="5">[and moreover,</t>
    <t s="6">from the fact that Yom HaKippurim is "k'Purim"</t>
    <t s="7">(with only the comparative letter kaf),</t>
    <t s="8">it is proven</t>
    <t s="9">that Purim is loftier than Yom Kippur10].</t>
    <t s="10">And the connection between Yom Kippur and Purim is,</t>
    <t s="11">that in both there is the matter of the lot.</t>
    <t s="12">For on Yom Kippur they cast a lot upon the two goats11,</t>
    <t s="13">and also Purim is named after the pur, which is the lot.</t>
    <t s="14">And another matter in the connection of Purim and Yom Kippur,</t>
    <t s="15">that both are above the name Havayah12.</t>
    <t s="16">For regarding Yom Kippur it is written13</t>
    <t s="17">"Before Havayah you shall be purified,"</t>
    <t s="18">[meaning] above Havayah14.</t>
    <t s="19">And also regarding Purim it is known15</t>
    <t s="20">that the reason the name Havayah is not mentioned in the entire Megillat Esther16</t>
    <t s="21">is because in Purim there is a revelation of Ein Sof that is above Havayah.</t>
  </section>
</awtsmoosMeluketTranslation>
